intended_object: The universal (generic) point of the upper-unitriangular group scheme U_n. It is the matrix of coordinate functions (x_ij), seen as an element of GL_n(O(U_n)), where O(U_n) is the coordinate ring. Inferred from the docstring, the module documentation (Milne 2.9) and the lemmas that follow (`universal_upper`, `universal_diag`).
explanation:
O(GL_n) is defined as K[x_ij][1/det], and its universal element is the invertible matrix (x_ij). The coordinate ring O(U_n) is the quotient of O(GL_n) by the ideal generated by the x_ij with j < i and by x_ii − 1. This definition pushes the universal GL matrix forward along the quotient map using `Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.map`, which gives the matrix (x̄_ij) in GL_n(O(U_n)). That is exactly the generic point of U_n. The lemmas right after it confirm the expected properties: the matrix is upper triangular, its diagonal entries are 1, and its entries are the images of the coordinates.

The generality is natural: any commutative base ring K and any finite linearly ordered index set ι. The order is needed to say "upper triangular". Mathlib has no unitriangular group scheme or coordinate ring, so there is no counterpart.
